questions.q: According to the stoics, what two outlooks cause anxiety?
a: Fearing what might happen or hoping too hard for something
Working too much or resting too little
Comparing yourself to others or hiding your talents
Avoiding decisions or rushing into them
questions.why: Lesson 1 says anxiety comes from great fears about the future or very high hopes.

questions.q: How might a stoic recommend facing a fear?
a: Experience the worst case so it loses its power
Distract yourself until the feeling passes
Talk it over with a trusted friend
Replace it with a more hopeful thought
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests embracing fears head-on, even briefly tasting the worst scenario.

questions.q: What did Lao Tzu's reaction to the vinegar show?
a: He found life sweet when accepted as it is
He thought life was sour and unfair
He believed suffering was the only truth
He refused to taste what others offered
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the vinegar ceremony to contrast Lao Tzu's sweet view with the others.

questions.q: What does Lao Tzu compare life to?
a: A body of water, calm beneath a chaotic surface
A road that must be walked quickly
A garden that needs constant pruning
A mountain that rewards hard climbing
questions.why: Lesson 2 says life is turbulent on the surface but peaceful and harmonious underneath.

questions.q: What did Jane Jacobs think made a city healthy?
a: Dense, mixed streets where people watch out for each other
Tall towers with private, separated communities
Wide highways connecting suburbs to downtown
Large parks with few shops or homes nearby
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Jacobs wanted cities to work like vibrant, mixed ecosystems.
